function: Learns AP-device association and device transmit power to minimize the aggregation MSE of over-the-air federated learning in a user-centric cell-free network (p. 1-2).
system: User-centric cell-free uplink with M=10 single-antenna APs and K=5 single-antenna devices, MRC at the edge server, imperfect CSI, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 2, 4).
method: Two-level hierarchical deep reinforcement learning: SAC for AP-device association, MAAC with CNN policies for per-device power control; normalized inputs and rewards (p. 3).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh fading with Gaussian estimation errors, APs and devices uniform in a 100 m circle; FEMNIST and Fed-CIFAR100 for the FL task (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation in one simulated environment (M=10, K=5); convergence curves repeated for other CSI error, M and K, no stated transfer (p. 4-5).
baselines: SAC-MADDPG (MAAC replaced by MADDPG in the hierarchical framework), centralized SAC for both decisions, particle swarm optimization (PSO), and the MSE-free ideal case (p. 4).
metrics: Average episode reward, log of average episode MSE, and OTA-FL training accuracy on FEMNIST and Fed-CIFAR100 (p. 4).
complexity: Time and space complexity of the ADA and PC agents stated in words (layer neuron products, buffer sizes), without O() expression or numbers (p. 3).
openness: none; FEMNIST and Fed-CIFAR100 are public learning datasets, no code or link released (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "modeled as Rayleigh fading" in a custom simulator (APs and devices placed in a 100 m circle); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "Fig. 5 shows the scalability of our algorithm concerning the numbers of APs (M) and devices (K)." The figure shows training convergence per setting (caption: "The convergence under different numbers of APs and devices"); no trained agent is tested in a new condition.
q3_support: p. 4: "This is a traditional DRL approach, where a centralized SAC outputs both ADA and PC decisions." and "Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is used to make ADA and PC decisions." Compared on MSE (Fig. 2) and training accuracy (Fig. 3).
q4_support: p. 3: "depends on the sum of the neuron products of each layer and scales with the number of training iterations" is part of a time and space complexity analysis of the ADA and PC agents, given in words only.
q5_support: p. 4: "We consider two datasets [12]:" FEMNIST and Fed-CIFAR100 are datasets of the learning task only; the channels are simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: Area 7: the learned agents minimize the over-the-air aggregation MSE (p. 1-2). AP association is above the physical layer but power control is physical, so the work passes above_phy. APs and devices have one antenna each, but M APs combine jointly with MRC (distributed MIMO), so the system exclusion was not applied. q3 to confirm: PSO (non-learned) and centralized SAC (standard DRL, same problem) are compared; SAC-MADDPG is a variant of the proposed framework, and no earlier published OTA-FL aggregation design is compared. q4 to confirm: the complexity is described in words, with no O() expression or numeric cost.
